proxy_compatibility.description: Direct compatible_pairs remain evidence-backed source-of-truth pairs. Named gameplay groups may use complete within-group compatibility or explicit group links, avoiding hundreds of enumerated proxy pairs.

group_links.note: Gameplay proxy for semi-aquatic pond/river turtles occupying water/moat space around arboreal/island primates. Supported by modern mixed-exhibit examples including squirrel monkeys/sakis with Yellow-Spotted Amazon River Turtles and Omaha primate/turtle exhibits. Excludes snapping turtles and other high-risk/specialist aquatic turtles from this broad proxy.

Gameplay proxy grounded in repeated modern lemur+tortoise exhibits, especially Ring-Tailed Lemur with Radiated/African Spurred Tortoise. This is an extrapolation for Zoo Curator, not a claim that every real-life individual/species mix is automatically safe.

Strong Zoo Curator gameplay proxy based on repeated modern Amazon/tropical-house exhibits. Lincoln Park Zoo explicitly mixes Yellow-Spotted Amazon River Turtle with Hoffmann's Two-Toed Sloth, White-Faced Saki and Golden-Headed Lion Tamarin; Omaha reports the turtle with Common Squirrel Monkey and sakis; Budapest reports Hilaire's Side-Necked Turtle with tamandua and emperor/golden-headed lion tamarins.

Broad gameplay proxy for non-predatory pond/river turtles using the water/moat layer of large mammal/primate exhibits. Supported by repeated zoo practice and specific modern examples, but intentionally excludes snapping turtles, softshell turtles and specialist/predatory aquatic turtles from the pond_turtles group.

Broad Zoo Curator proxy supported by modern mixed wetland exhibits. Eurasian Spoonbill is housed with Chilean Flamingo at Dublin Zoo; Roseate Spoonbill with Caribbean/American Flamingo at Toledo Zoo; African Spoonbill with Greater Flamingo in the successful Odense Zoo African waterbird aviary.

Broad wetland-bird proxy. Odense Zoo successfully bred African Spoonbill and Pink-Backed Pelican together; other modern collections repeatedly hold spoonbills and pelicans in mixed wetland assemblages.

Broad wetland-bird proxy anchored by the successful Greater Flamingo + Pink-Backed Pelican Odense Zoo mixed aviary. Pelican predation on eggs/chicks can occur, so this represents viable exhibit cohabitation rather than zero-risk breeding compatibility.

Large-public-aquarium gameplay proxy. Modern public aquaria routinely maintain selected sharks and rays together in very large systems. Species selection and feeding remain important; freshwater rays and Tiger Shark are excluded from this broad rule.

Zoo Curator gameplay proxy anchored by a published Parma Wallaby + Patagonian Mara compatibility study at Dudley Zoo. Apply to low-conflict open-ground macropods/maras; individual husbandry still matters.

Broad tropical-house proxy: agoutis repeatedly occupy the terrestrial layer below sloths and small/medium New World primates. Supported by white-faced saki husbandry reports and modern South American walkthrough exhibits.

Broad ground-vs-arboreal gameplay proxy anchored by Cleveland Metroparks Zoo's 2018 mix of Southern Three-Banded Armadillo with Linne's Two-Toed Sloth, Golden Lion Tamarin, Goeldi's Monkey and White-Faced Saki.

Directly supported by modern tropical-house records, including Hoffmann's Two-Toed Sloth with a Dasyprocta agouti at CREA (2024) and Linne's Two-Toed Sloth with Dasyprocta leporina in BioParque do Rio.
Supported by Cleveland Metroparks Zoo (Linne's Two-Toed Sloth + Southern Three-Banded Armadillo, 2018) and Chelyabinsk Zoo (Linne's Two-Toed Sloth + Six-Banded Armadillo, 2010).

Zoo Curator rule: modern Golden Lion Tamarin + two-toed sloth evidence extends to the full tamarins gameplay group. Smithsonian documents Golden Lion Tamarins and two-toed sloths as long-term exhibit mates; Cleveland Metroparks also documents Golden Lion Tamarin + Linne's Two-Toed Sloth.

Zoo Curator rule: modern Golden Lion Tamarin + armadillo evidence extends to the full tamarins gameplay group. Cleveland Metroparks Zoo documented Golden Lion Tamarin + Southern Three-Banded Armadillo in the same 2018 mixed exhibit.

Zoo Curator rule: Golden Lion Tamarin + agouti evidence extends to the full tamarins gameplay group. Jerusalem Biblical Zoo documented Golden Lion Tamarin + Dasyprocta leporina in 2007; Houston Zoo describes Golden Lion Tamarins sharing a mixed habitat with red-rumped agoutis.

Requested Zoo Curator gameplay proxy. Capuchins share broadly similar arboreal/omnivorous ecology and mixed-primate husbandry precedents. Tufted capuchins have especially strong mixed-species evidence. This does not claim that every capuchin species pair is routinely co-housed in real zoos; introductions, sex composition and escape/refuge design still matter.

Requested Zoo Curator gameplay proxy. Mixed macaque exhibits have real institutional precedent, including a long-running National Zoological Park association involving Barbary, lion-tailed and Sulawesi macaques. Because macaques can be socially assertive and closely related species may hybridize, this is a gameplay compatibility rule rather than a blanket real-world husbandry recommendation.

gameplay_notes.pond_turtle_proxy_caution: This is a Zoo Curator gameplay abstraction, not husbandry advice. EAZA European Pond Turtle guidelines warn against indiscriminate reptile mixing and note competition/disease risks. The broad proxy is therefore limited to selected non-predatory pond/river turtles and low-conflict mammals occupying different habitat layers.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_final_pass: Final Tropical Birds evidence pass. Added modern named-zoo mixed-exhibit records for hornbills/turacos, South American macaws/aracaris, and selected cross-category partners. Broad Goeldi's Monkey + parrot/Amazon compatibility is an explicit Zoo Curator gameplay proxy requested by the designer, grounded in a 2024 EAZA multi-zoo survey documenting Goeldi's Monkey with Green-cheeked Parakeet and Golden Conure; it is not a claim that every listed parrot species has been directly exhibited with Goeldi's Monkey.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_caution: No blanket toucan/aracari, turaco, or hornbill complete-group proxy was added. These taxa can show aggression/predation/territoriality in mixed aviaries, so only documented combinations or existing specifically approved proxies are used.
gameplay_notes.new_level4_carnivora: Added Common Kusimanse (Crossarchus obscurus) and Egyptian Mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon) as Level 4 Carnivora. Direct named-institution compatibility: Common Kusimanse + Blue-Eyed Black Lemur (Memphis Zoo), Common Kusimanse + Diana Monkey (Newquay Zoo). ZooRope also documents Common Kusimanse with Hystrix cristata and Atherurus africanus, but these are not mapped to Cape Porcupine (Hystrix africaeaustralis). Egyptian Mongoose + White-tailed Mongoose is documented at Samjung The Park (2016), but White-tailed Mongoose is not in the current Zoo Curator roster.
gameplay_notes.marine_mania_pass_2026_09_19: Marine Mania pass added structured compatibility for flamingos, spoonbills, pelicans, selected penguins, pinnipeds, sharks and rays. All six Zoo Curator flamingos are a complete gameplay group. Spoonbills are a complete group and broadly link to flamingos and pelicans. Pelicans are grouped, but notes retain the real husbandry caveat that pelicans may take eggs/chicks. Cold-water mixed penguin group is Gentoo, King, Rockhopper, Macaroni and Chinstrap, supported by modern Edinburgh/Detroit/Newport/Loro Parque exhibits. Humboldt, African and Magellanic penguins are NOT blanket-grouped: Spheniscus hybridisation is documented, including Humboldt x Magellanic, and husbandry guidance advises against indiscriminate Spheniscus mixing. Shark/ray grouping is deliberately limited to selected marine public-aquarium species; freshwater Ocellate River Stingray and Xingu River Ray and high-risk Tiger Shark are excluded from the broad proxy.
gameplay_notes.other_mammals_pass_2026_09_19: Other Mammals pass focused on maras, agoutis, wallabies/kangaroos, two-toed sloths and armadillos. Maras, agoutis and selected ground macropods are gameplay groups; existing two-toed sloth and armadillo complete groups remain. Broad links use habitat-layer logic where modern zoo evidence supports repeated terrestrial/arboreal coexistence. Patagonian Mara has numerous direct modern mixed-exhibit anchors with capybara, rhea, anteater, camelids, tapir and Parma Wallaby. Sloth/agouti/armadillo links are anchored by Cleveland Metroparks Zoo, CREA, BioParque do Rio, Smithsonian and Chelyabinsk records. Tree-kangaroos, koala, wombat, echidna, platypus, Tasmanian devil and other specialists are NOT folded into a blanket Australian-mammal rule.
gameplay_notes.tamarin_group_extrapolation_2026_09_19: Designer-confirmed Zoo Curator rule: credible lion-tamarin compatibility for two-toed sloths, armadillos or agoutis extends to every member of the named tamarins gameplay group. Explicit group_links make this rule deterministic.
gameplay_notes.ungulates_continued_and_other_birds_pass: Continuation pass added 98 new direct evidence-backed pairs, prioritising post-2000 named-institution mixed exhibits. Other Birds were cross-linked only where the source describes actual co-housing/mixed habitat; conceptual exhibit plans and generic taxonomic assumptions were excluded. Kori Bustard care guidance was used as a caution source but not converted wholesale into direct pairs because named-institution evidence was preferred. Crane/stork combinations were not blanket-proxied because compatibility is species- and exhibit-dependent.
gameplay_notes.other_birds_antwerp_aviary_2026_09_19: Added 33 direct pairs from Antwerp Zoo Cape Buffalo Aviary, opened 2016 and documented by ZooLex in 2020. ZooLex explicitly states that keeping birds and Cape Buffalo together has proven unproblematic and lists the bird community sharing the aviary. This is treated as direct named-institution evidence, not a blanket taxonomic proxy.
gameplay_notes.other_birds_continued_2026_09_19: Continued Other Birds evidence pass. Added exact named-institution cohabitation from Gaiapark Kerkrade (2006), Tiergarten Schoenbrunn (2024), Dierenpark Zie-ZOO, and Dusit Zoo (2010), plus successful Kori Bustard combinations listed by the AZA Kori Bustard Care Manual. Kori aggression-listed combinations (Grey Crowned Crane, Common Ostrich, Marabou Stork, Saddle-Billed Stork) were deliberately not added from that manual. No blanket stork/crane/ibis/bustard proxy was created.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_asset_refresh_2026_09_19: Updated Tropical Birds level assignments per designer list. Compatibility is species-based and independent of card level. Added new named-institution evidence found during refresh; existing complete macaw/parrot/amazon gameplay groups retained. Duplicate Papuan Hornbill at Level 3 was deduplicated in inventory. Rufous Hornbill remains listed at both Level 4 and Level 5 because the supplied level list conflicts and no level was silently chosen.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_continued_v2_6: Added direct cohabitation records from RIO Ekzoopark (2016), Wildlife Rescue Center No.1 Nakhon Nayok (2024), Pattaya Crocodile Farm (2012), and Bergzoo Halle via ZooRope. Bergzoo Halle entries are treated as one documented mixed-exhibit community. No blanket hornbill, toucan/aracari or turaco complete-group proxy was introduced.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_continued_v2_7: Rotterdam Zoo's Congo Forest - Birds and Okapis explicitly lists Okapi, Hoopoe, Western grey plantain-eater, Violet turaco and Green turaco in the same mixed-species aviary. Zoo Curator names Common Hoopoe and Western Plantain-Eater are used for those roster taxa. Only missing direct pairs were added. EAZA turaco guidance cautions that mixed-turaco outcomes can depend strongly on species, breeding state, timing of introductions and enclosure design, so no blanket turaco complete-group rule was created.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_continued_v2_8: Adds only direct evidence-backed combinations. Palm Cockatoo manual reports Long-billed Corella and Blue-eyed Cockatoo as successful but cautions Palm Cockatoos can become aggressive, particularly while breeding; therefore these are direct pairs only, not a cockatoo proxy. Sharjah Safari's 2024 walk-through aviary supplies an actual named-institution community for African Grey Hornbill, Great Blue Turaco, Demoiselle Crane, Hadada Ibis, Hamerkop, Allen's Gallinule and African Pied Hornbill.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_continued_v2_9: Audubon Zoo's official Wings of the World page lists Curl-crested Aracari, Umbrella Cockatoo, Hyacinth Macaw and Toco Toucan as highlights of the exotic aviary; missing pairwise combinations were added. San Diego Scripps Aviary evidence was used conservatively only to connect African Grey Parrot to exact Zoo Curator bird taxa reported in that aviary, rather than making all aviary inhabitants mutually compatible.
gameplay_notes.tock_hornbill_review_v3_0: Von der Decken's Hornbill was reviewed conservatively. Dwarf Mongoose remains strongly supported by multiple zoo institutions plus the species' well-known natural mutualism. Rock Hyrax and Violet Turaco retain direct named-institution evidence. Meerkat was removed despite positive Smithsonian evidence because a later Henry Vilas Zoo report describes meerkats killing a female Von der Decken's Hornbill; this fails Zoo Curator's thriving/viable-combination standard. Red-Billed Hornbill gained direct pairs with Dwarf Mongoose (Nürnberg/Oregon), Meerkat and Rock Hyrax (Basel), Klipspringer (Lincoln Park Zoo 2024), and Hamerkop (Aalborg Zoo mixed exhibit).
gameplay_notes.hornbill_safety_pass_v3_1: v3.1 reviewed remaining hornbills for both successful and problematic mixes and added/removed no direct pairs.
gameplay_notes.tropical_birds_continued_v3_2: Mo & Mo (2021) review documents zoo combinations of adult Green Iguanas with Channel-billed, Toco and Keel-billed Toucans; Blue-and-yellow, Scarlet and Military Macaws; and Yellow-crowned, Yellow-headed and Yellow-shouldered Amazons. The paper cautions that toucans can prey on juvenile Green Iguanas, so these direct pairs represent appropriately managed adult mixed exhibits, not unrestricted breeding/juvenile safety. Emerald Toucanet + Green Iguana was not added in this pass because the review's cited examples trace to pre-2000 reports, below Zoo Curator's preferred evidence threshold. Dallas World Aquarium's 2013 Orinoco exhibit directly documents Plate-billed Mountain Toucan + Golden Lion Tamarin.
gameplay_notes.toucan_aracari_deep_pass_v3_3: Dallas World Aquarium was searched at exhibit level rather than treating its very large ramphastid collection as automatically compatible. The April 2013 Jungle Junction record explicitly describes six toucan taxa sharing one exhibit with Giant Anteater; Zoo Curator taxa from that community were added pairwise. A 2021/22 review independently records Giant Anteater, Toco Toucan and Black-Necked Aracari in Jungle Junction. The Orinoco free-flight records support Crimson-Rumped Toucanet and Chestnut-Eared Aracari with Scarlet Ibis and with each other. The DWA Toucan Terrace webpage and Zootierliste/Zooinstitutes holdings were not interpreted as proof that every listed species cohabits. No blanket toucan/aracari proxy was added.
gameplay_notes.tamarin_sloth_deep_pass_v3_4: Added exact direct evidence for Golden Lion Tamarin + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth and Green Aracari at Smithsonian; Cotton-Top Tamarin + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth at Yekaterinburg Zoo (2019); Bearded Emperor Tamarin + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth in Smithsonian Amazonia (2019); and Golden-Headed Lion Tamarin + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth in Colchester's Rainforest Walkthrough. These direct records strengthen the existing gameplay-level tamarin extrapolation but do not replace it. Bird Park Marlow (2024) documents Black Lion Tamarin with Linne's two-toed sloth, White-faced saki and Lilacine Amazon; this was not inserted because Black Lion Tamarin is not currently an exact species key in this compatibility file. Smithsonian's 2015 Golden Lion Tamarin community also independently confirms sloth, saki and three-banded armadillo; already-existing pairs were not duplicated.
gameplay_notes.tamarin_sloth_deep_pass_v3_5: Taipei Zoo's official Pangolin Dome page states that Cotton-top Tamarin, two-toed sloth, Scarlet Ibis and Great Curassow are free-ranging, supporting direct pairs among those exact Zoo Curator taxa. Houston Zoo's 2010 Natural Encounters mixed exhibit documented Cotton-top Tamarin, Golden Lion Tamarin, White-faced Saki, two-toed sloth and Red-footed Tortoise together (plus non-roster/uncertain taxa); missing exact-roster pairs were added. Duisburg's ZooInstitutes mixed exhibit directly lists Cotton-top Tamarin with Green Iguana and larger hairy armadillo; only the exact Zoo Curator Cotton-top + Common Green Iguana pair was added. The 2021 peer-reviewed Green Iguana review independently reports Cotton-top Tamarins as the most frequently documented tamarin/iguana combination across numerous institutions, though it also records occasional adverse interactions; this remains a managed direct pair, not a blanket tamarin-iguana proxy.
gameplay_notes.tamarin_sloth_evidence_deep_pass_v3_6: Cotton-top Tamarin + Southern Three-banded Armadillo is directly supported by Tierpark Hellabrunn's 2024 official announcement of a renovated shared enclosure. A 2023 peer-reviewed study of Callimico welfare documents a 2780 m3 South American walkthrough containing Goeldi's Monkey, Golden-headed Lion Tamarin, Southern Two-toed Sloth and Southern Tamandua; only missing exact-roster pairwise links were added. Brevard Zoo's current official account independently confirms Goeldi's Monkey living with White-faced Saki, Golden-headed Lion Tamarin and Linne's Two-toed Sloth. Emperor Tamarin + Azara's Agouti has unusually strong 2022/2023 evidence (Parc d'Isle feeding-interaction study; Lakeland Wildlife Oasis 2020), but was NOT mapped onto Zoo Curator's Red-rumped Agouti because these are different species. Likewise, the 2002 Cotton-top Tamarin + Black-rumped Agouti association was retained only as research context, not converted to Red-rumped Agouti. This pass deliberately strengthens direct evidence beneath the tamarin gameplay extrapolation without broadening the proxy rules.
gameplay_notes.tamarin_sloth_agouti_armadillo_deep_pass: Houston Zoo's current official Golden Lion Tamarin page explicitly places Golden Lion Tamarins, howler monkeys and Red-rumped Agoutis in one mixed habitat. Auckland Zoo officially announced that its incoming Cotton-top Tamarin pair would be joined by Red-rumped Agouti. A November 2024 Stone Zoo species list identifies Cotton-top Tamarin, Linne's Two-toed Sloth and Red-rumped Agouti as one exhibit, providing an independent modern record. Oglebay Good Zoo has a photographed 2023 exhibit containing Linne's Two-toed Sloth, Golden Lion Tamarin, Southern Three-banded Armadillo and Red-footed Tortoise. Cleveland Metroparks Zoo's 2018 named mixed exhibit and Zoo Schwerin's 2024 named mixed exhibit were re-expanded pairwise to catch any missing exact-roster links. Despite these positive records, no general tamarin↔agouti proxy was created: husbandry discussion reports agoutis can injure or kill tamarins, especially young animals. Thus only directly documented managed combinations remain eligible. Minnesota Zoo's 2005 annual report independently confirms Cotton-top Tamarin + Southern Three-banded Armadillo and Golden Lion Tamarin + Linne's Two-toed Sloth + Green Aracari, but those direct pairs were already present and were not duplicated.
gameplay_notes.agouti_grouping_v3_8: Per explicit Zoo Curator design instruction, all agoutis are treated as functionally equivalent for gameplay compatibility. The existing 'agoutis' proxy group now contains every agouti/acouchy taxon represented in the compatibility dataset and is listed in complete_groups. This means members inherit the same group-level compatibility links. Direct species-level pairs remain untouched as the auditable evidence layer. This is an intentional gameplay extrapolation rather than a claim that all agouti species have identical published husbandry records.
gameplay_notes.red_footed_tortoise_deep_pass_v3_9: Houston Zoo's August 2010 Natural Encounters record explicitly documents Cotton-top Tamarin, Golden Lion Tamarin, White-faced Saki, Red-footed Tortoise and two-toed sloth within the same nine-species exhibit; missing exact-roster links were added. Primate Report 64 documents Goeldi's Monkey + Red-footed Tortoise as an association since 2000 and states no problems and that the association is recommended. Dublin Zoo's official current Red-footed Tortoise page explicitly says the tortoise shares its habitat with White-faced Saki. A 2015 Tropicarium Budapest photograph independently documents Cotton-top Tamarin + Red-footed Tortoise (plus Crested Wood Partridge) in one enclosure. Buffalo Zoo's recent peer-reviewed mixed-primate study independently confirms White-faced Saki + Red-footed Tortoise in the shared exhibit. No broad tortoise↔tamarin proxy was created: evidence remains species/exhibit specific.
gameplay_notes.south_american_rainforest_deep_pass_v4_0: The 2021 peer-reviewed Green Iguana review is now used more fully for exact Zoo Curator taxa: Golden Lion Tamarin, Golden-headed Lion Tamarin, White-faced Saki, Linnaeus's Two-toed Sloth and Southern Tamandua all have documented Green Iguana co-housing. The 2024 multi-zoo Callimico survey independently records Goeldi's Monkey mixed with Red-rumped Agouti, three-banded armadillo, Green Iguana, Red-footed Tortoise, two-toed sloth and several callitrichids; only previously missing direct pairs were inserted. Roger Williams Park Zoo's 2025 exhibit-level inventory distinguishes free-ranging Golden Lion Tamarin, Linnaeus's Two-toed Sloth, Red-footed Tortoise and Scarlet Ibis from its separate Southern Tamandua + Keel-billed Toucan enclosure, so those structures were preserved rather than flattening the whole building into one compatibility clique. Bioparque do Rio's 2021 big walkthrough explicitly contains Green Iguana, Linnaeus's Two-toed Sloth and Red-rumped Agouti. The complete agouti gameplay group from v3.8 remains intact, but direct pairs continue to record exact evidence.
gameplay_notes.reptiles_african_tortoises_v4_1: ZooRope documents Dierenpark Zie-ZOO's Meerkat + Rock Hyrax + Leopard Tortoise + African Spurred Tortoise mixed exhibit, plus African Spurred Tortoise with Meerkat/Cape Porcupine at Rotterdam and Dwarf Mongoose at de Paay, and Leopard Tortoise with Dwarf Mongoose at Doué-la-Fontaine. Parc Merveilleux documents Fennec Fox + African Spurred Tortoise. Sharjah Safari has a 2024 Ring-tailed Lemur + Radiated Tortoise exhibit; Zoo Leipzig officially describes Crowned Lemur + Radiated Tortoise together in Gondwanaland. The 2021 peer-reviewed Green Iguana review explicitly reports successful or managed co-housing with Rhinoceros Iguana, adult Boa Constrictor, Burmese Python and Red-footed Tortoise. Boa and python combinations are retained as direct evidence but should be understood as high-management mixes because the paper notes predation risk and adult/well-fed snake conditions. No broad tortoise, snake or iguana proxy groups were created.
gameplay_notes.pond_slider_pond_turtle_deep_dive_v4_2: Pond Slider is treated at species level (Trachemys scripta), so evidence for red-eared, yellow-bellied or Cumberland sliders can support the Zoo Curator Pond Slider card. Under explicit user instruction, a slider documented as sharing a tropical hall, large pond or mixed-species community with another exact Zoo Curator taxon is enough to add the pair. This pass therefore includes American Alligator, Green Iguana, macaws, peccary, American Black Bear, Capybara, Giant Anteater, tropical-house parrots and several freshwater turtles. European Pond Turtle is not given the same blanket treatment: EAZA's 2021/2023 Best Practice Guidelines warn against mixing reptiles/amphibians from different geographic areas and against species occupying the same niche. For Emys orbicularis this pass therefore adds only directly documented shared Zürich Selenga wetland taxa. A 2026 Zie-ZOO visitor correction was also checked carefully: the big lake animals are Pond Sliders, not European Pond Turtles, so Capybara and Giant Anteater were deliberately NOT assigned to European Pond Turtle from that source. Follow-up searching found the requested primate crossover directly: Tropicarium Budapest's 2015 enclosure held Golden-headed Lion Tamarin + Green Iguana + Red-eared Slider. Chattanooga Zoo's 2025 exhibit also documents Red-eared Slider + White-tailed Deer. A 2022 Réserve Africaine de Sigean exhibit additionally documents Bolivian Squirrel Monkey + American Alligator + Red-eared Slider, but Bolivian Squirrel Monkey was not inserted because it is not currently represented as an exact species key in this compatibility dataset.
gameplay_notes.pond_slider_maximal_followup_v4_3: A second dedicated search expanded Pond Slider again under the user's permissive shared-exhibit/tropical-hall rule. New exact-roster direct pairs include Cuvier's Dwarf Caiman, Spectacled Caiman, Yacare Caiman, Tufted Capuchin, Patagonian Mara, Greater Rhea, Roseate Spoonbill and Scarlet Ibis. The crocodilian additions are based on actual shared enclosures rather than mere co-occurrence in a reptile house. The Sendaviva 2020 exhibit is particularly strong primate evidence: Black-capped Capuchin (Zoo Curator's Tufted Capuchin), Capybara and Red-eared Slider are photographed as one mixed exhibit. Oceanogràfic's official Wetlands Aviary supports treating its Red-eared Slider as compatible with the large aviary birds under the explicit tropical-hall/walkthrough rule. A historical Woodland Park Zoo record also had West African Dwarf Crocodiles with a Red-eared Slider, but it predates 2000 and therefore was not used to create a new direct pair under the project's evidence standard. Réserve Africaine de Sigean's 2022 Bolivian Squirrel Monkey + American Alligator + Red-eared Slider exhibit remains a research lead because Bolivian Squirrel Monkey is not an exact current Zoo Curator key.
gameplay_notes.caiman_grouping_v4_4: The managed_caimans proxy group contains Cuvier's Dwarf, Smooth-fronted, Spectacled, Yacare and Broad-snouted Caiman. It is intentionally NOT listed in complete_groups, so the game should not infer that every caiman can live with every other caiman. Instead, group-links allow Pond Slider and Common Green Iguana compatibility to extrapolate across this managed caiman set. That extrapolation is based on multiple real zoo combinations: Pond Slider is directly documented with Cuvier's, Spectacled and Yacare; Green Iguana is published with dwarf/Paleosuchus caimans, Smooth-fronted Caiman and Spectacled Caiman. Black Caiman is excluded because its size/predatory risk profile is materially different and available evidence does not justify treating it like the smaller/medium managed caimans. Direct caiman-caiman evidence is retained separately: Cuvier's + Spectacled at Johnsons of Old Hurst, and Smooth-fronted + juvenile Broad-snouted at Belo Horizonte. St. Augustine Alligator Farm 2026 adds Cuvier's Dwarf Caiman with Arrau River Turtle and Yellow-spotted Amazon River Turtle. This is a gameplay compatibility proxy, not a claim that every member is behaviorally identical.
gameplay_notes.caiman_capybara_turtle_deep_pass_v4_5: Temaiken provides unusually strong evidence: a photographed 2010/2011 enclosure explicitly held Broad-snouted Caiman, Yacare Caiman and Capybara together; a 2013 photo independently shows Yacare Caiman with Capybara, and a 2025 report says the resident broad-snouted caiman had lived with capybaras for much of its life. These are retained as direct pairs rather than turning Capybara into a managed_caimans group-link, because young capybaras remain plausible prey and the evidence does not yet cover the smaller Paleosuchus species. Connecticut's Beardsley Zoo documents Yacare Caiman + Mata-Mata in the same pool. Barcelona's documented reptile mixes add Cuvier's Dwarf Caiman with West African Black Forest Turtle, Neotropical Painted Wood Turtle, South-East Asian Box Turtle and adult Red-footed Tortoise, plus Chinese Alligator + Giant Asian Pond Turtle. Blue Planet Aquarium's current official exhibit independently adds Cuvier's Dwarf Caiman + Geoffroy's Side-necked Turtle. No full crocodilian proxy was created, and managed_caimans remains non-complete.
gameplay_notes.crocodilian_turtle_deep_pass_v4_6: Berlin Zoo Aquarium provides unusually clear post-2000 crocodile-to-crocodile evidence: Nile Crocodile, Cuban Crocodile and Orinoco Crocodile are all explicitly listed in the same 2006 mixed exhibit, so all three pairwise links were added. Spectacled Caiman + Branderhorst's Snapping Turtle was added because the turtles were reported to have bred in the shared exhibit, which is stronger evidence than simple co-location. Dwarf Crocodile + West African Mud Turtle was added from a documented San Antonio Zoo mix. Smithsonian's current Reptile Discovery Center was checked but its species list alone does not prove which taxa share individual enclosures, so no pairs were inferred from that page. A current 2026 Siantar Zoo Saltwater Crocodile + False Gharial mix was also found but deliberately excluded: contemporary observers explicitly flag the arrangement as potentially dangerous, and this project excludes combinations where the available evidence points to an unsafe mix. Morelet's Crocodile and False Gharial are reported with 'numerous turtle species' at Vienna facilities, but those claims were not converted because exact Zoo Curator turtle species were not identified. managed_caimans remains non-complete and Black Caiman remains excluded.
gameplay_notes.gharial_turtle_false_gharial_v4_7: Indian Gharial is now intentionally one of the strongest crocodilian+turtle mixers in the database. San Diego Zoo's 2011/2013 Gharial and Turtles exhibit explicitly held gharial with Pig-nosed/Fly River Turtle, Malaysian Giant Pond Turtle, Malaysian Painted River Turtle, Red-bellied Short-necked Turtle, Spotted Pond Turtle and Chinese Stripe-necked Turtle. Bronx JungleWorld provides independent modern support for gharial with Asian forest/brown tortoise and giant Malaysian/Asian pond turtles, and WCS stated in 2017 that its new gharials entered a river already occupied by Asian turtles and fish. Haus des Meeres was treated more conservatively than the user's Pond Slider tropical-hall rule: only species explicitly described as sharing the Crocodile Park enclosure were added. This gives False Gharial direct links to Bearded Barbet and White-crested Turaco. The same enclosure contains additional starling/bulbul taxa not currently exact Zoo Curator keys. No complete gharial or crocodilian proxy group was created.
gameplay_notes.reptile_mixed_exhibit_sweep_v4_8: This pass broadens beyond crocodilians while retaining all prior caiman/gharial work. Zoo Negara's published False Gharial breeding account directly supports False Gharial + Asian Water Monitor in the same large enclosure. Toronto contributes a Burmese Star Tortoise + Asian Giant/Brown Tortoise + Spiny Hill Turtle community and Black Tree Monitor + Red-bellied Short-necked Turtle. hedgehog_reasoning: Long-eared Hedgehog has direct post-2000 mixed-exhibit evidence with White-rumped Seedeater at Rotterdam (2009) and Common Scops Owl at Moscow (2011), showing the species is not intrinsically unsuitable for mixed exhibits.

Long-eared Hedgehog is a small nocturnal arid/semi-arid insectivore; Lesser Hedgehog Tenrec is convergently similar but taxonomically unrelated and needs warmer husbandry. The group is therefore a gameplay/husbandry extrapolation, not a claim of close relatedness.

Partner propagation is limited to already-established small-insectivore mixed-exhibit partners (Meerkat and Aardvark); no blanket compatibility with every partner of every hedgehog/tenrec is asserted.
manatee_findings: Dallas World Aquarium 2010 gives an exact roster pair: West Indian/Antillean Manatee + Arrau River Turtle.

Duisburg officially confirms West Indian Manatees share the Rio Negro water area with Arapaima, rays and other South American fish; its tropical hall also has free-ranging Red Titi, Golden Lion Tamarin, Southern Tamandua and two-toed sloth, but these are not automatically treated as sharing the manatee's aquatic enclosure.

Burgers' Zoo currently keeps West Indian Manatees and Red Titi in the same Mangrove ecosystem. This supports ecosystem-level coexistence, but the available official wording does not prove direct shared access to the manatee pool, so no Manatee + Red Titi direct pair was added.

Beauval's Equatorial Dome contains manatees, squirrel monkeys, golden lion tamarins, turtles and many other species, but the official page describes multiple separate pools/spaces; co-location in the dome alone is not enough for a direct pair.

A planned but unrealized combination is not compatibility evidence, so Platypus remains uncovered.

research_pass_notes: v6.3 coati/meerkat/raccoon/skunk pass: added 17 exact Zoo Curator pairs backed by named-institution mixed-exhibit records. Unknown-institution-only records were excluded. Meerkat already had very broad coverage (42 pairs), so this pass concentrated on under-covered coatis, raccoons and skunks.

v6.4 Burgers' Zoo mixed-exhibit pass. Added direct official-zoo evidence from Burgers' Desert and Rimba. This includes Black-Tailed Prairie Dog + North American Porcupine, several Rimba hoofstock/siamang links, and Turkey Vulture links where Burgers explicitly describes free-flying Desert birds as able to enter the peccary, porcupine and prairie-dog enclosures. No pairs were inferred merely because species occur in the same ecodisplay.

v6.5 focused Dutch-zoo pass: Diergaarde Blijdorp, ARTIS, Ouwehands Dierenpark and Apenheul. Added Blijdorp Nepalese Red Panda + Tufted Deer; ARTIS Red Ruffed Lemur + Radiated Tortoise; Apenheul Black-Headed Spider Monkey + Capybara. Ouwehands' clearly documented Zoo Curator matches (including Meerkat + Common Warthog and the gorilla/meerkat/turaco mix) were already represented, so they were not duplicated. Removed Asian Small-Clawed Otter + South American Coati: Apenheul's historical trial ended after serious aggression, so it does not meet the project's 'viable/thriving combination' standard.

v6.6 focused pass: Chester Zoo, London Zoo, Tierpark Berlin, Zoo Berlin and Zoo Plzeň. Added 12 new exact Zoo Curator pairs. Chester's strongest documented matches (e.g. Aardvark + Meerkat and Grevy's Zebra + Common Ostrich) were already present, so no duplicate Chester pairs were added. London added Humboldt Penguin + Rockhopper Penguin and White-Faced Saki + Southern Tamandua. Tierpark Berlin added missing links from its African Savannah plus Asian Small-Clawed Otter + Sulawesi Babirusa. Zoo Berlin added South American Tapir + Visayan Warty Pig from the Rhino Pagoda. Plzeň added the three pairwise links among Capybara, Vicuña and Lesser Rhea from its current shared South American Pampas exhibit. No species proxy was used where the exact Zoo Curator animal was absent.

v6.7 ZooChat credibility pass. ZooChat was treated as an observational lead source, not as automatic proof. Added only posts that identify a real zoo and an actual mixed exhibit, with preference for recent inventories, long-standing members, photographs, or repeated institutional reports. Speculative 'would this work?' combinations were excluded. Failed/dangerous mixes were excluded. Exact Zoo Curator taxa were required; no loose species proxies were introduced. This pass added Whipsnade rhino mixes; Berlin Zoo mixes; Chester orangutan/gibbon mixes; Ouwehands, Wildlands and Overloon links; detailed US primate exhibits; London Rainforest Life links; several named-zoo armadillo mixes; and well-established giant-anteater combinations.

v6.8 targeted low-coverage ZooChat pass. Searched mixed-exhibit threads for named-institution observations rather than speculative proposals. Added only exact Zoo Curator taxa not already represented as direct pairs. Older reports were accepted only when they described an actual exhibit; recent 2024–2025 observations were preferred where available. Several plausible reports were left out where the exact taxon could not be matched safely to a current card.

v6.9 targeted cleanup/expansion: normalized the typo 'Black-Tailed Prairie Dog' to 'Black-Tailed Prairie Dog' throughout the JSON and deduplicated normalized direct pairs. Added Asian Elephant + Blackbuck (documented at Dublin/Zurich) and Asian Elephant + Red Deer (Dierenrijk) while retaining the existing Asian Elephant + Crab-Eating Macaque evidence. Added complete gameplay proxy groups for capuchins and macaques at the user's request. The existing parrots and spider_monkeys complete groups already provide the requested taxonomic same-group compatibility, so they were preserved rather than duplicated. Proxy rules are explicitly labelled as gameplay extrapolations, not claims that every pair is a documented zoo mixed exhibit.

v7.4 focused tamarin/marmoset/armadillo/two-toed-sloth audit. Added modern named-institution direct pairs: Bearded Emperor Tamarin + Six-Banded Armadillo (CERZA, 2025); Golden-Headed Lion Tamarin + Southern Three-Banded Armadillo (Zoo Brno, 2025); Pygmy Marmoset + Southern Three-Banded Armadillo (Allwetterzoo Münster, 2025); Common Marmoset + Large Hairy Armadillo and + Six-Banded Armadillo (Bridlington Animal Park, 2024); Geoffroy's Tufted-Ear Marmoset + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth (Woodside Wildlife Park, 2024); Large Hairy Armadillo + Linnaeus's Two-Toed Sloth (Parco Natura Viva, 2024); Cotton-Top Tamarin + Large Hairy Armadillo (Spaycific'Zoo, reported 2011). Existing gameplay group-links already make all named tamarins/marmosets compatible with the armadillo and two-toed-sloth groups; this pass strengthens the direct evidence layer without pretending every cross-pair has its own zoo record.
